title: Portkey AI Gateway: a header-configured recursive LLM request router
purpose: Route each inbound OpenAI-shaped request through a per-request, header-supplied target tree (single/fallback/loadbalance/conditional) with retries, timeouts, caching and guardrail hooks, holding no state between requests.

interface.entry: POST /v1/chat/completions and the other OpenAI-shaped endpoints (src/index.ts:135-220)
interface.request: OpenAI JSON body plus x-portkey-config or x-portkey-provider, plus x-portkey-{retry-count,request-timeout,metadata,trace-id,cache,custom-host} (src/middlewares/requestValidator/index.ts:111, src/globals.ts:13)
interface.response: provider response verbatim plus x-portkey-last-used-option-index (the config JSON path), x-portkey-retry-attempt-count, x-portkey-cache-status, x-portkey-trace-id, x-portkey-provider (src/handlers/services/responseService.ts:99)
interface.config: a recursive schema: strategy{mode,on_status_codes,conditions,default}, targets[], weight, retry{attempts,on_status_codes,use_retry_after_header}, cache{mode,max_age}, request_timeout (src/middlewares/requestValidator/schema/config.ts:14, :53)

model_selection.property: The model named in the request body is the model sent upstream, unless the selected target declares override_params, which are merged over the body and win.
model_selection.guarantee: No quality or price scoring, no aliases, no escalation ladder: resolution is a pure object merge evaluated per target, so a fallback target may legitimately serve a different model than the primary, and the caller is not told.

placement.property: Placement is declarative: fallback takes targets in declaration order, loadbalance draws one target at random in proportion to its weight, conditional matches predicates over metadata, body and URL to a named target, single takes the first.
placement.guarantee: Weights are never normalised, a missing weight becomes 1, and selection is one draw over the raw sum followed by cumulative subtraction. No latency, queue-depth, in-flight or affinity signal exists anywhere in the router.

admission_and_overload.property: The gateway never queues and never refuses on its own capacity judgement; it always attempts the chosen target and forwards whatever the upstream says.
admission_and_overload.guarantee: No admission control, concurrency cap, queue or drop policy exists. A rejection is the upstream's verdict, either retried or passed through; the only self-generated refusals are 446 for a guardrail denial, 408 for its own timeout, and a 500 tagged with the gateway's exception marker.

rate_limit_pacing.property: Quota is not modelled at all: exhaustion is discovered only by being rejected, after which the router either backs off exponentially or, when configured to, sleeps the provider-supplied delay.
rate_limit_pacing.guarantee: No request or token counter, no pre-call estimate, no headroom reserve. A provider-supplied wait is honoured only while the accumulated wait stays under 60000 ms; a longer one aborts retrying immediately. A rate limiter exists in the tree but is imported by no file.

retry_and_fallback.property: Same target first, different target second: a configured number of extra calls to the same endpoint on the listed status codes, then the fallback loop advances to the next target in config order.
retry_and_fallback.guarantee: Attempts default to 0, so retries are off unless asked for; the default retry status set is 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, and applies only once attempts exceed 0. The schema puts NO upper bound on attempts and the shipped maximum-retries constant is never referenced. Back-off is a 1 s / 2 s / 4 s ladder with randomisation explicitly disabled, so there is no jitter. A non-listed non-2xx bails with zero retries; with no status list a fallback group diverts on ANY non-2xx including 400 and 401.

outage_and_health.property: not decided: there is no health state. Every request evaluates its chain from scratch from the config in its own headers, so a target that failed the previous thousand requests is tried again at full weight.
outage_and_health.guarantee: The only two health touchpoints are a filter on a config-supplied flag and an optional host-injected callback, and nothing in this repository ever sets either. The only process-global mutable state is the optional response cache, the admin sessions and the log clients.

deadline_and_priority.property: The only time notion is a per-attempt timeout in milliseconds, resolved header first, then target config, then inherited config, then off.
deadline_and_priority.guarantee: It aborts an in-flight upstream call and synthesises a 408, but the timer is cleared as soon as response headers arrive, so it bounds time to first byte and NOT a streaming body. It is per attempt, so the worst case is (attempts+1) times the timeout plus back-off. There is no deadline field, no priority tier and no slack-aware ordering.

tenant_isolation.property: not decided: there is no tenant. Identity arrives as an opaque per-request config header and nothing is accounted, budgeted or reserved per caller.
tenant_isolation.guarantee: No per-caller quota, share or noisy-neighbour handling. Worse, the response cache is keyed on the transformed request body and the endpoint name only, with no caller, provider or organisation mixed in, so one caller's cached completion can be served to another.

cost_control.property: not decided in this repository: cost is a seam, not a policy. A host-injected validator may reject a request before the upstream call and hand back a pricing record, which is only copied into the log.
cost_control.guarantee: With nothing injected the service is a no-op and spend is bounded only by traffic: no price table, no cheapest-first selection, no spend counter. Every retry and every fallback hop issues a fresh billable upstream call with no compensating accounting.

policy_state_and_determinism.property: The routing policy is a pure function of the request body, the config header, the wall clock and one unseeded random draw: no learning, no per-session cache, no carry-over between requests.
policy_state_and_determinism.guarantee: Replay is reproducible for single, fallback and conditional and NOT reproducible for weighted selection: the draw is unseeded and only the resulting config path is reported. Per-request state grows with the chain, one guardrail span and one log record per target attempted. Cross-request state is limited to the optional response cache, a module-level object with no size bound that evicts only on an expired read.

decision_observability.property: The chosen target is reported as the exact config JSON path in a response header, alongside the attempt count, cache status, trace id and provider; every attempt including abandoned retries emits its own log record.
decision_observability.guarantee: The attempt count is -1 when the budget was exhausted without success, which is deliberately not the number of attempts made. The gateway's own exceptions collapse to a generic 500 with the detail only on standard error. A streamed response is logged as a placeholder string, so streamed traffic cannot be audited after the fact.
